stem: The rate of the reaction $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$ is studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A small amount of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ is mixed with a large excess of $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ at a temperature of $400\text{ K}$ and the reaction is monitored. The graph obtained is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why a large excess of $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ is used in this experiment.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The reaction is first order with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$.

Use data from the graph to confirm this statement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Three separate experiments were carried out at $400\text{ K}$ with different starting concentrations of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$. The results are shown in the table.

| experiment | $[\text{H}_2\text{(g)}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{I}_2\text{(g)}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | rate of reaction $/\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $1.0 \times 10^{-2}$ | $1.0 \times 10^{-2}$ | $2.0 \times 10^{-17}$ |
| 2 | $1.0 \times 10^{-1}$ | $1.0 \times 10^{-1}$ | $2.0 \times 10^{-15}$ |
| 3 | $5.0 \times 10^{-1}$ | $5.0 \times 10^{-1}$ | $5.0 \times 10^{-14}$ |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Use the data, and the order of reaction with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ given in (a)(ii), to deduce the order of reaction with respect to $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$.

Explain your answer, giving data in support of your explanation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use information from (a)(ii) and your answer to (b)(i) to write the rate equation for the forward reaction.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your rate equation and data from experiment 1 to calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$, for the forward reaction at $400\text{ K}$. Include units for $k$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
At $400\text{ K}$ the rate constant for the forward reaction is approximately 1000 times greater than the rate constant for the backward reaction. The overall orders of the forward and backward reactions are the same.

forward reaction $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HI(g)}$
backward reaction $2\text{HI(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)}$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Use this information to explain what will happen if equal concentrations of $\text{HI(g)}$, $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ are mixed at $400\text{ K}$.

You should comment on:
- the relative initial rates of the forward and backward reactions
- the position of the equilibrium reached.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
At $700\text{ K}$ the rate constant for the forward reaction is approximately 50 times greater than the rate constant for the backward reaction.

Use this information and the information in (c)(i) to deduce the signs of the $\Delta H$ values of the forward and backward reactions. Explain your answer.
